_comment: Free-tier SHAPE per vendor, not numbers.
Why there are no numbers here: every vendor publishes its limits in a table
that is rendered from live account data, so any number baked into an APK is
wrong within weeks — and a wrong limit is worse than no limit, because the
user plans around it. So this file records only what IS stable and was
verified against the vendor's own documentation (see 'verifiedAt'):
- which dimensions the vendor measures (rpm / rpd / tpm / tpd / ...),
- whether an API endpoint reports a counter we can read instead of counting,
- whether free models are marked in the model id.
The app tracks usage locally (it knows every request it sent) and compares
against a limit the user enters once from their own dashboard. Where a vendor
exposes a counter endpoint, that is read instead — see 'counter' below.

limits.note: Groq measures RPM, RPD, TPM, TPD, ITPM, OTPM and audio-second limits, all at once — the first one hit is the error you get. Limits are per model AND per key, so two keys are two independent budgets.
Gemini evaluates RPM, TPM and RPD together and applies them per PROJECT, not per key — two keys from the same project share one budget. RPD resets at midnight Pacific.

counter.note: OpenRouter reports the free-model daily counter itself. Reading it is strictly better than counting locally: it includes requests made from other devices on the same key.

limits.note: Free models are the ids ending in :free. The daily cap depends on lifetime credits purchased, so the number is per-account and only the account page or /api/v1/key knows it.
Measured in requests and tokens per minute plus tokens per day.
Vercel bills a monthly credit, not a daily request count. Some catalogue models carry a $0 price and consume nothing — those are the ones worth grouping as free.
The free tier is capped per second and by a monthly token allowance, not per day.
The allowance is set by the account's Copilot plan, so only the account page states it.
Developer credits are consumed per request rather than reset daily.
A small monthly credit on the free plan, with per-provider limits underneath.
No free daily allowance; the platform limits how many requests may run at once.
Rate limits are set per model.
